questions.q: What is the key difference between a program and a process?
options: There is no difference; the terms are interchangeable
A program is a file on storage doing nothing; a process is a running instance of it with its own memory and PID
A process is a file; a program is a running instance of it
A program can only run once; a process can run many times
questions.explain: A program is a file sitting on storage. The moment it's launched, the OS creates a process: it allocates memory, assigns a PID, and schedules CPU time.

questions.q: What happens when running processes collectively request more memory than a machine has available?
options: Nothing; RAM expands automatically to meet demand
The CPU slows down its clock speed permanently
The OS may swap data out to slower disk, or terminate processes to free space
Storage is automatically converted into RAM
questions.explain: RAM is finite. When demand exceeds supply, the operating system swaps memory to disk (much slower) or kills processes to free space — the classic "out of memory" failure mode.

questions.q: Why does data in storage survive a reboot while data in RAM does not?
options: Storage is persistent memory; RAM is volatile and loses its contents when power is lost
RAM is actually faster at retaining data than storage
Storage requires a constant power supply to retain data
There is no real difference between RAM and storage
questions.explain: RAM is volatile (temporary) memory that empties when power is cut. Storage (SSD/HDD) is persistent and keeps its contents through a reboot or power loss.

questions.q: On a Northbridge Retail checkout server running a point-of-sale app, a background sync job, and OS housekeeping tasks simultaneously, what are each of those three running as?
options: Three separate programs, with no processes involved
Three separate processes, each with its own memory, sharing the same CPU and RAM
A single process split across three machines
Three copies of the same storage file
questions.explain: Each running instance is its own process with its own isolated memory and PID. Multiple processes share the same underlying CPU and RAM via the OS scheduler.

questions.q: What is the practical value of being able to read a process list (Task Manager, Activity Monitor, or `top`/`ps`)?
options: It lets you edit a program's source code directly
It quickly shows which process is consuming excessive CPU or memory, a day-one server troubleshooting skill
It permanently deletes unwanted processes from storage
It replaces the need for an operating system
questions.explain: A process list shows each process's ID, CPU usage, and memory usage, making it easy to spot the one process hogging resources — a core diagnostic skill for running servers.
